rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Mucor, the pin mould, builds a coenocytic mycelium of sporangiophores, stolons and rhizoids; it spreads asexually by thousands of sporangiospores released from columella-bearing sporangia and survives hard times as a thick-walled zygospore made by conjugation of + and − strains.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
The columella inside a Mucor sporangium is sterile. Spores are cut from the cytoplasm around it. Plus and minus strains are both required for the zygospore in the usual heterothallic account.
Yeast in the absence of oxygen turns glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide. That is fermentation. The sexual spores, usually four, sit in an ascus, which is the cell itself after fusion and meiosis.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Sporangiospore vs ascospore:** sporangiospores form asexually inside a sporangium (Mucor); ascospores form sexually after meiosis inside an ascus (yeast).  ·  **Zygospore vs ascus:** the zygospore is a thick-walled diploid resting structure; the ascus is a sac in which meiosis produces haploid spores.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Match the organism to the character.  ·  A product does not move an organism into another kingdom.

rows.text: ***Mucor mucedo*** — the classic pin mould of bread and dung.  ·  ***Saccharomyces cerevisiae*** — baker's and brewer's yeast.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Rhizoids down, stolons across, sporangiophores up" — Mucor's three hyphae.  ·  "4–8 in the ascus" — yeast ascospore count.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What is a columella? **Answer.** The **dome-shaped sterile dome** inside the *Mucor* sporangium — the swollen tip of the sporangiophore pushing up into the spore mass, separating it from the fertile sporangiospores and supporting them.  ·  **Short answer (2m):** What is a zygospore? **Answer.** The **thick-walled, dark, diploid resting spore** formed when the gametangia of **+ and − mating strains** of *Mucor* conjugate. It survives drought and unfavourable seasons, and on germination undergoes **meiosis** to start a new haploid mycelium.

rows.text: Most-tested: sporangiospore formation, conjugation, budding, fermentation equation.

rows.text: - Three kinds of hyphae: · Hypha | Direction | Function · **Sporangiophores** | Upright, aerial | Bear sporangia at their tips (asexual) · **Stolons** | Horizontal along the surface | Spread the colony · **Rhizoids** | Downward, branched root-like | Anchor and absorb; secrete enzymes  ·  Mucor — structure and reproduction classified · Feature | Detail | Exam note · Habitat | Saprophytic on bread, dung, moist organic matter | 'Pin mould' from the pin-like sporangiophores · Mycelium | Coenocytic, branched; rhizoids anchor, sporangiophores rise | Three hypha types: rhizoids, sporangiophores, runner hyphae · Asexual reproduction | Sporangium at each sporangiophore tip → thousands of sporangiospores | Fastest coloniser of fresh substrate ·…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Two dispersal strategies:** asexual spores for rapid identical spread; sexual spores (zygospore/ascospores) for survival and recombination.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Mucor: coenocytic mycelium with sporangiophores, stolons, rhizoids; asexual sporangiospores with columella; sexual conjugation of +/− strains → zygospore (resting spore).  ·  Yeast: unicellular ascomycete, vacuolate eukaryotic cell; asexual budding (and fission); sexual conjugation → ascus with 4–8 ascospores after meiosis; haplodiplobiontic cycle.  ·  Yeast fermentation: zymase converts glucose → ethanol + CO₂ + energy; basis of bread and brewing.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Buchner (1897) showed cell-free yeast extract ferments sugar — the enzyme zymase; birth of enzymology.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ***Schizosaccharomyces octosporus*** — fission yeast, 8 ascospores.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Budding vs binary fission:** budding produces an unequal bud (yeast); fission divides the cell into two equal halves (Schizosaccharomyces, bacteria).  ·  **Rhizoid vs root:** rhizoids are fungal anchoring filaments — no vascular tissue, no root cap, no organs.  ·  Diagrams carry this topic: Mucor mycelium with the three hypha types + sporangium with columella; yeast budding chain + ascus.

rows.label: More ideas
